required_outcomes: Does not treat the inspection as finished with nothing to do: the landlord's email raises two new matters (an unapproved dog flap and a spare front door key after a lock change) and both get a recorded follow-up action.

Raises the dog flap as its own follow-up (a new request or task): establish with the tenant what was installed and when, and put the decision on keeping, removing or making good to the landlord, rather than handling it inside the completed inspection.

Addresses the key question directly: finds out who changed the lock and when, arranges for a spare key to be provided to the landlord or agency, and tells the landlord what the record does and does not show (this case records no lock change).
Replies to the landlord acknowledging both points and stating what will happen next.
acceptable_alternatives: One follow-up request that lists both items clearly, instead of two separate ones.
Escalating the dog flap decision (consent, removal, cost at end of tenancy) to a human once the facts have been gathered from the tenant.
positive_behaviours: Notes that the inspection report said no issues were identified while the landlord reports a dog flap, and flags the discrepancy for the inspector without accusing anyone.

Links the dog flap to the tenancy agreement's alterations and pets clauses and to the dog already mentioned in the record (events 006 and 007), and keeps the tone with the tenant courteous and factual.
Treats a lock change without the agency or landlord holding a key as an access and safety matter to resolve promptly, not just a question to answer.
red_flags: Replies to the landlord that the inspection is closed with no issues and takes no further action.
Tells the tenant to remove the dog flap or hand over keys immediately on the landlord's say-so, before any facts are established.
prohibited_actions: Instructing a contractor to remove the dog flap or change the locks before the landlord has decided and the tenant has been contacted.
Closing the case with no follow-up recorded for either item.
critical_failures: Dismissing the landlord's email and leaving both the dog flap and the missing key with no action recorded anywhere.
